subject: Maths
title: 3 times table
subtitle: Multiplication and Division (3, 4, 8 Times Tables) · KS3 Maths
learning_objective: I can recall and use the 3 times table to multiply and divide.

key_vocab.definition: The 3 times table is a list of multiples of 3: numbers we get when we count in 3s. The digits of every multiple of 3 add up to a multiple of 3 (e.g. 27 → 2+7 = 9).

sections.title: Learning Objective
sections.content: I can recall and use the 3 times table to multiply and divide.

sections.title: Key Words
sections.content: 3 times table -- The 3 times table is a list of multiples of 3: numbers we get when we count in 3s. The digits of every multiple of 3 add up to a multiple of 3 (e.g. 27 → 2+7 = 9).

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
Multiplication is repeated addition. 3 × 4 means ‘4 groups of 3’. You can also think of it as ‘3 groups of 4’ — the answer is the same.
3 + 3 + 3 + 3 = 3×4 = 12
Four groups of 3

Key examples:
  ✓ 1 × 3 = 3  (starting point)
  ✓ 2 × 3 = 6  (double)
  ✓ 5 × 3 = 15  (halfway to 10)
  ✗ 3 × 3 = 10  (wrong)
  ✗ 3 × 0 = 3  (any × 0 = 0)

sections.title: Worked Example
sections.content:
Example 1 – single multiplication
  Calculate 7 × 3
  7 groups of 3
  3 + 3 + 3 + 3  ...
  = 21
  = 21
  (Skip-count in 3s 7 times to reach 21.)

Example 2 – missing factor
  Solve: ___ × 3 = 15
  How many 3s in 15?
  Count up: 3, 6, 9, ...
  = 5
  = 5
  (Divide: 15 ÷ 3 = 5.)
